description:
She smuggled 2,500 children past the Nazis — hidden in suitcases, coffins, and ambulances.

Irena Sendler was a Polish social worker who, working with the underground resistance group Żegota, smuggled approximately 2,500 Jewish children out of the Warsaw Ghetto during World War II. She wrote each child's real name on tissue paper, sealed the lists in glass jars, and buried them under an apple tree — so families could reunite after the war.

Arrested by the Gestapo in October 1943, tortured, and sentenced to death, she never revealed a single name.
